exercise intensity modulates hepatic lipid metabolism in a dose-dependent fashion.

the effects of exercise on hepatic metabolism in the healthy and diseased state.

The main takeaway from our work is that

high intensity interval exercise training is a promising strategy that may lead to a reduction in liver fat content, and to a modulation in the hepatic lipid metabolism in obese and cancer cachexic subjects.

high intensity interval training (HIIT) has a profound impact on hepatic lipid metabolism, and that this is a result of the activation of AMPK, which in turn activates PPARα, and that the effects of HIIT are even more prominent in disease, as is obesity and cancer cachexian.
